title: Shared browser inspection
summary: Browser inspection SHOULD run as a tab in the one shared headless Chrome for Testing instance. It MUST never borrow the operator's personal browser identity, and MUST leave no page, browser process, or host setting behind.
instructions: Agents SHOULD run browser inspection and Visual QA as a tab in the one shared, long-lived headless Chrome for Testing instance on `http://127.0.0.1:9222`. They attach to it through a `chrome-devtools` MCP server started with `--browserUrl=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. That server carries no `--isolated`, `--executablePath`, or `--headless` flag. When no such server is available, an agent MAY drive the same instance directly over its DevTools port. This path is a preference: it keeps one browser on the machine and no window on the desktop.
On the shared instance, each agent MUST open its own tab with `new_page` under a unique `isolatedContext` name. It MUST reuse that tab with `navigate_page` and MUST NOT launch a browser of its own.

An unavailable Chrome for Testing bundle, shared instance, or `chrome-devtools` server MUST NOT block browser inspection. The agent MUST record the gap in case evidence and continue with another browser automation tool that keeps the rules of this policy. Examples are the Playwright MCP server and a headless Chromium the agent launches with a throwaway profile. The agent MUST stop every browser it launched when inspection finishes, including on failure.

Every browser path MUST stay headless or in the background. Agents MUST NOT bring any browser window to the foreground or rely on a visible window. A visible browser window on the operator's desktop is a defect to report. Agents MUST NOT attach to the operator's personal browser, use its profile, or drive automation through the personal `com.google.Chrome` identity.
Agents MUST close every page they open when inspection finishes, including on failure.
Agents MUST NOT print or persist a session token or cookie value. Such values stay inside the page.
Agents MUST NOT change macOS Launch Services, the default browser, or Chrome preferences as remediation. Agents MUST NOT kill or quit all MCP Chrome processes as the primary remediation.

Enforcement of the preceding prohibition is mechanical, not advisory. The operator's `beforeShellExecution` hook `~/.cursor/hooks/deny-browser-env-write.py` denies shell commands that rebind the `http`/`https` handlers or write the Launch Services handler database. The same hook denies commands that mutate the personal Chrome preference domain or profile tree, or kill a browser by name. Read-only diagnosis stays available. The operator MUST authorise a genuine repair and prefix the single command with `ALLOW_BROWSER_ENV_WRITE=1`. An agent MUST NOT set that variable for itself, and MUST report the block instead.

Case evidence MUST record which browser path ran and why. It MUST also record every browser automation action, DOM observation, `isolatedContext` confirmation or the fallback's isolation evidence, and every page close.

`pan doctor` reports whether the Chrome for Testing bundle is present and whether the server attaches over `--browserUrl`. Agents MUST treat a gap in that report as an advisory, and it MUST NOT block a browser verdict.

When no browser tool that keeps this policy is reachable, a stage that owes a browser verdict MUST report the case as environment-blocked. It MUST NOT convert the gap into a product pass or fail. It MUST NOT substitute a screenshot or capture fallback for a required browser verdict.
Design exploration and iteration MAY use a disclosed non-browser capture fallback, because it produces craft feedback rather than a verdict.
When one stage already owns browser inspection for a surface, another stage MUST NOT duplicate it. That stage MUST record its own verification and reference the existing evidence.
A brief for a subagent that may open a browser MUST name `BROWSER-001` and carry its instructions.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you open a browser page or record a browser verdict.
